comments.note: The pmRefreshTab function fully re-renders the tab content on every interaction (edit, done, cancel, collapse). For the current scale (20+ personas across 3 suites) this is acceptable and consistent with the mrRefreshTab pattern in the Model Registry tab. If performance becomes an issue with larger persona sets, targeted DOM updates (toggle display:none on individual edit/display elements) could replace the full re-render for the common edit/cancel path.

The pmDoRebuild function passes the initial page-load 'assignments' parameter through the entire callback chain. After a successful rebuild, re-fetched data is stored in pmAssignments (module-level) and pmPersonas, so rendering is correct. However the closure chain becomes slightly confusing because the 'assignments' param from the outer scope is never the fresh data — it's always the initial page load value. A minor clarity improvement would be to eliminate the 'assignments' parameter from the pm* functions entirely and rely solely on module-level state.

config.js now has three parallel tab implementations (General, Persona Models, Model Registry) each with their own module-level state variables and refresh pattern. The General tab uses a simpler stateless pattern, while the two new tabs follow a mrModels/pmModels local-state pattern. As the file grows, extracting each tab into its own file (views/config-general.js, views/config-persona-models.js, views/config-model-registry.js) with a thin dispatcher in config.js would significantly improve maintainability.

summary: QA FAIL — AC #7 violated: rebuild failure output is not shown in the <pre> block. Build passes (TypeScript compiles), all 3523 existing tests pass (no regressions), but a server/client contract mismatch causes the rebuild error message to display 'HTTP 500' instead of actual build output. 10 of 11 ACs are confirmed implemented correctly via code review. One AC is unmet.

comments.note: AC #7 FAIL — Rebuild error output not shown in <pre> block. Root cause: server.ts sends `sendJson(res, 500, { success: false, output: '...', exitCode: N })` for a failed rebuild (exit code != 0). The api-client.js `request()` function handles non-2xx responses by reading `errData.error.message`, but the rebuild failure response body is `{ success: false, output: '...', exitCode: N }` — it lacks the `error.message` field. So `errMsg` falls back to `'HTTP 500'`. The `pmDoRebuild` catch block then puts `err.message` (= `'HTTP 500'`) into the `<pre class="pm-build-error-pre">` block instead of the actual script output. Fix options: (A) Change `server.ts` line ~1895 to `sendError(res, 500, 'BUILD_FAILED', result.output, port)` so the output is in the standard `error.message` field; or (B) in `pmDoRebuild` catch, additionally try parsing the raw response body for `output` field. Option A is cleanest and consistent with all other error handling.

pmDirtyDot() reuses the Model Registry's `.mr-dirty-dot` CSS class instead of a dedicated `.pm-dirty-dot`. This works but is a mild coupling concern — if mr-dirty-dot styles change they affect the Persona Models tab too. Low risk since both tabs want the same visual style.

pmDoRebuild() after success updates `pmAssignments.stale` from freshAssignments but does not merge `freshAssignments.persona_models` or `freshAssignments.default_model_uuid` back into `pmAssignments`. This is by design (rebuild doesn't alter assignments), but worth documenting explicitly in the function comment to avoid future confusion.

summary: Rework: fixed server/client contract mismatch in POST /api/personas/rebuild error path. Changed server.ts lines 1895–1896 from `sendJson(res, 500, result, port)` to `sendError(res, 500, 'BUILD_FAILED', result.output, port)`. The rebuild failure response now uses the standard error envelope `{ error: { code, message } }` that api-client.js already parses — so `err.message` in pmDoRebuild's catch block now carries the actual build script output, which is displayed in the `<pre class=\"pm-build-error-pre\">` block. TypeScript build passes, all 3523 regression tests pass.

comments.note: The fix is minimal and correct. No new observations beyond those already recorded in the first implementation pipeline. The server.ts rebuild handler is now consistent with all other error paths in the file — failure results use sendError() with a structured envelope rather than bare sendJson() with a non-standard shape.

comments.note: Fix-Forward: `pmDirtyDot()` in config.js (line 289) was using `.mr-dirty-dot` — the Model Registry's CSS class — for the Persona Models tab's dirty indicators. This is a cross-tab coupling: any future restyling of `.mr-dirty-dot` would silently affect the Persona Models tab. Applied fix: added `.pm-dirty-dot` as a selector alias to the `.mr-dirty-dot` ruleset in styles.css (both selectors share the same declaration block), then updated `pmDirtyDot()` to emit `.pm-dirty-dot`. The visual output is identical; QA validation is unaffected. The two tabs are now visually decoupled.

The `pmWireEvents` function signature carries `config, models, personas, assignments` parameters that are never directly consumed by the function body — they are passed through to `pmRefreshTab` which in turn passes them recursively into the next `pmWireEvents` call. The actual rendering reads from module-level state (`pmModels`, `pmPersonas`, `pmAssignments`). This closure pass-through is the Developer-documented debt. It creates a confusing interface but causes no bugs today. When extracting pm* into its own file, eliminating these parameters entirely (relying solely on module-level state) would be the correct simplification.

In `pmDoRebuild` (lines 780–783): on success, `pmRefreshTab(config, models, pmPersonas, assignments)` is called where `pmPersonas` has just been updated (correct) but `assignments` is the stale initial page-load value. This is safe because `pmRefreshTab` ignores the `assignments` parameter — it reads `pmAssignments` (module-level) directly via `pmBuildTabHtml()`. The parameter is a vestigial pass-through. The Developer's own implementation comment notes this; no behavioral issue exists, but future readers may be confused by seeing `assignments` (old value) passed next to `pmPersonas` (new value).

[documentation-forward] `pmDirtyDot()` now emits `.pm-dirty-dot`; the `api-surface.md` or `ui-components.md` documentation should note that both `.mr-dirty-dot` and `.pm-dirty-dot` share the same CSS declaration block in styles.css — so a single restyling of that block affects both tabs. This prevents a future contributor from adding per-tab dirty-dot overrides in the wrong place.

[documentation-forward] The `pmWireEvents` function's parameter signature (`config, models, personas, assignments`) is architecturally misleading — these params are pass-throughs, not inputs. A brief doc comment on the function should explain that the function body reads from module-level pm* state and that the parameters exist solely for the pmRefreshTab recursive closure chain. This would prevent future contributors from incorrectly routing logic through these parameters instead of module-level state.
